title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
version_designed_for: NARROWER NON-VENTURE VERSION named in G34-score.json narrower_version_if_borderline: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema plus TAK Server extension (ICS 201/204/209/214 and a resource/LOGSTAT-style ledger as CRDT-merged Data Sync mission objects) with an ATAK-CIV plugin and an iOS/web companion, stewarded with the TAK Public Safety community and the WFTAK/COTAK state wildland programs, monetized through hosting/support subscriptions to state wildland agencies and incident management teams. The Guard line is kept ONLY as an unfunded drill-weekend credibility test, the allied line ONLY as an optional 2028 DIANA application, and the 'license the merge model' revenue line is DROPPED (commoditized by Automerge/Yjs/Ditto). Verdict was KILL as a venture; this plan therefore treats G34 as a bootstrappable open-source-plus-hosting business whose 90 days must answer one decisive doubt: does ANY named agency, state TAK program or IMT with a budget line pay for structured offline ICS objects rather than using free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS? Every milestone below tests that doubt with a measurable kill criterion. This is not a venture-scale company and the plan does not pretend it is.

links.value: Incident command posts, field divisions and higher coordination centers that already run TAK on unclassified networks still carry assignments (ICS 204), status (ICS 209/214) and resource/sustainment status as paper, chat, voice and spreadsheets; when nodes reconnect after working disconnected, edits made in parallel do not merge and staff re-key by hand, so the picture diverges between ICP, field and higher.
links.detail: FACT that TAK Data Sync re-syncs map items/files/chat but carries no structured form objects and no multi-writer merge (Google Play Data Sync listing, TPC; OpenTAKServer Mission API docs 2025-2026). FACT that public-safety TAK use is routine (DHS S&T/HS Today; WFTAK; Green Bay Fire + FirstNet 2025). INFERENCE that the disconnected multi-writer conflict is episodic rather than daily (score file criterion 1 = 3/5); the daily pain is form re-keying per operational period. Severity is tolerated today.

links.value: Incident commander, planning section chief, resource unit leader and situation unit leader on Type 1-3 incident management teams; state wildland fire dispatch/technology leads running WFTAK or a state TAK program (COTAK, Colorado); municipal fire TAK administrators; secondary: National Guard battalion S3/S4 and battle captain on state active duty (unfunded credibility test only).
links.detail: FACT: WFTAK is an interagency TAK server developed by the Colorado Center of Excellence under agreement with FAM IM Tools & Technology; wildland responders are ~80% iOS (wftak.wildfire.gov). FACT: COTAK runs a 2026 COTAK Summit (cotak.gov schedule page surfaced 2026-09; date not verified - .gov blocked). FACT: Guard units use ATAK on domestic missions (nationalguard.mil ATAK video; CivTAK National Guard archive) but no Guard requirement for structured offline reports found - Public evidence insufficient.

links.value: No single requirement owner. Each agency/IMT sets its own; NWCG (National Wildfire Coordinating Group) sets interagency wildland standards and hosts IM Tools & Technology/WFMRDA but does not buy; FEMA NIMS defines ICS form standards but does not buy; for the Guard, no validated requirement exists (Public evidence insufficient).
links.detail: FACT: NWCG provides national leadership for interoperable wildland fire operations among federal, state, local, tribal partners (nwcg.gov). FACT: NIMS ICS forms booklet is public FEMA guidance. INFERENCE: the closest thing to a requirement owner for a TAK-native ICS object schema is the WFTAK/COTAK program lead plus the TAK Public Safety 501(c)(3), neither of which controls budget. This is the first weak link.

links.value: None for the product. DHS S&T funds TAK development through the TAK Product Center (TPC), not agency purchases; WFTAK is operated by the Colorado Center of Excellence with FAM IM Tools; COTAK is Colorado's state TAK program; no Guard program office exists for a battalion orders/reports app.

money_map.weakest_link: BUDGET (tied with REQUIREMENT OWNER): there is no line item, program of record or requirement anywhere in the chain for structured offline ICS objects in TAK; the only money is a $1B+/yr grant pool spread across thousands of agencies with spending mandates that do not name this class, plus agency operating budgets. Without a named agency that will put a hosting/support subscription on a purchase order, every other link is decorative.
money_map.penalty_note: Chain penalty applies: the Guard segment has no requirement owner, program office, budget or vehicle (Public evidence insufficient), and the civil segment has a budget pool but no line. The score file's market attractiveness of 2.7 already reflects this; nothing found this session raises it. The FY2026 HSGP NOFO (June 2026) and CivTAK 2026 (Nov 18-20) are new, verifiable calendar facts, not new budget evidence.

procurement_signal.rationale: There is no government RFI -> sources sought -> prototype -> production sequence for this product because the civil buyer never runs one: public-safety incident management software is a mature, multi-vendor commercial category (DHS SAVER 2022, FACT HIGH) bought agency by agency on grants and operating budgets, and TAK itself is free government software whose sync layer (Data Sync) is already in production. The only formal procurement signals are on the military side (PM MC OMCS RFI, SBMC prototype awards, Onebrief follow-on) and those are being closed by funded incumbents, which is exactly why G34 retreated to public safety. The TAK-native structured-objects slice is 'Emerging' in the narrow sense that nobody ships it, but absence of a vendor is not evidence of demand; the recurring signals (annual HSGP NOFO, annual CivTAK/TAK Offsite, TAK Public Safety founded 2024) show a mature adoption curve for TAK in public safety, not a procurement pipeline for this feature. Confidence MEDIUM.

entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: No ownership test, no clearance, no ATO. ATAK-CIV and its SDK are open-source government software (E07-F25, FACT HIGH); confirm the ATAK-CIV license and any copyleft obligations before publishing (counsel). Product design must stay EAR99/publicly-available: publishing the core as open source generally removes it from EAR control as 'published' software, but this is a legal determination for export counsel, not a finding here. The Indonesian founder can work on this codebase (E07-F17: deemed-export licensing applies only to controlled technology). TAK-GOV/MIL builds remain distribution-controlled - do not touch them. CivTAK is open to the public; TAK Offsite Day 1 (CUI) is not open to foreign persons.

entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: No ownership test for direct commercial sales or OTS (E07-F22). SBIR/STTR (DHS, Army) is NOT available without a >50% U.S.-person-owned cap table (13 CFR 121.702) - counsel; STRATFI/TACFI are therefore also closed (they require SBIR Phase II lineage). Hosted service may trigger state security reviews, CJIS-adjacent questions and StateRAMP for some buyers - budget for it only after a paying customer asks. Register in SAM.gov and obtain a UEI early (federal), and register as a vendor with each state.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: The first revenue and the only metric that matters for the kill decision: paying agencies and ACV. If 12 months after CivTAK 2026 there are fewer than 3 paying agencies or ARR under $50k, the business is a hobby or an acquihire pitch, not a company.

questions: Walk me through the last operational period on your most recent large incident: from the planning meeting to the ICS 204s in the hands of division supervisors, who typed what, into what, and how many times was the same assignment re-entered?

The last time a division or strike team lost connectivity for hours, what happened to the status they collected while disconnected - how did it get back into the plan, and what was wrong or duplicated when it did?
Show me how resource status (ICS 214/215, T-cards, whiteboard, IMS) is reconciled at the end of a shift; who notices when two people changed the same record, and what do they do?
What does TAK actually show on your incidents today - PLI, markers, chat, data packages - and what still travels on paper, radio or a separate app? Why that split?
When you brief the IC or the agency administrator, which numbers do they distrust, and how do you defend them?
Which of your responders are on iPhones versus Android, and how do the iOS users get incident information today?

Tell me about the last software your agency bought for incident management: who proposed it, what money paid for it (grant, operating budget, P-card), how long from idea to purchase order, and who could have vetoed it?
If a free TAK plugin did structured ICS 204/214 forms tomorrow, what would have to be true for you to push it to your fleet - and who would have to approve it?
What did you stop using in the last three years, and why did it lose?
How do you exchange the incident action plan and status with the neighboring agency, the state EOC and the federal team that arrives on day three? Where does it get retyped?

For Guard interviewees: walk me through receiving the OPORD/FRAGO and reporting SITREP/LOGSTAT/PERSTAT on your last state active duty mission - what tools, what links, and what happened after each displacement or reconnect?
Who in your state or agency would you introduce me to that has actually paid for TAK-adjacent software, and who has refused to?
What does your training pipeline look like for TAK - who onboards a new user, how long does it take, and where do people give up?

first_deployment_path.path: Primary: a no-cost MOU pilot on one state wildland TAK program's server (WFTAK-using state or COTAK-type program) during pre-season training or a prescribed-burn period in Q1-Q2 2027, on the agency's own Android/iOS devices with the open-source extension deployed server-side and the web companion for iOS, measured against paper/IMS baseline in one operational period; secondary, unfunded: observe/test at one Guard battalion drill weekend or a state Vigilant Guard-series exercise using synthetic data only. No Project Convergence, NetModX, ANTX, Bold Quest or CWIX participation is pursued - those are military experimentation venues that require sponsors, CUI environments or NATO nation nomination this team cannot meet in 12 months and that address a buyer (Army/NATO) this version has abandoned.
first_deployment_path.evidence_it_produces: Field metrics (multi-writer edits made during a >=4-hour partition merge with zero re-keying and zero lost updates on both Android and iOS; ICS 204 production time versus baseline; bytes per object over mesh), a signed agency reference, and - the only evidence that matters - a written answer from the agency budget holder on whether and how they will fund hosting/support in FY2027. This evidence supports a bootstrapped revenue business or an acquihire conversation with Ditto, a TPC contractor (e.g., PAR Government) or an IMS vendor. It does NOT support a Series A, STRATFI (requires SBIR Phase II lineage this cap table cannot obtain) or a DIU production transition (no DoD requirement owner); stating otherwise would dress a niche business up as a venture.
alternatives: Municipal fire department pilot on FirstNet (connected majority): weaker test of the offline merge thesis but faster to arrange via TAK Public Safety chapters

IMS-vendor partnership pilot: offer the open-source TAK object layer as an integration to Tablet Command/Resgrid/Intterra for a joint customer - fastest route to an acquihire signal, slowest to independent revenue

DHS S&T SVIP Innovation OTS topic (if a first-responder situational-awareness topic opens in 2027): federal prototype dollars without an SBIR ownership test - RECALL LOW on international eligibility; monitor, do not plan around it
NATO DIANA 2028 cohort via a German-domiciled entity: EUR 100k and test-centre access; credibility, not deployment

allied_extension.bigger_with_allies: No - allies add a second small channel and credibility, not a larger market. DIANA's 2027 'operational resilience in contested environments' and 'responsive logistics' challenges match the problem statement almost verbatim (FACT, 2026-06-02) but the window closed 2026-07-03, awards are EUR 100k, and the next realistic target is the 2028 cohort with applications ~mid-2027 (pattern-based). Systematic SitaWare Edge already offers tasking in NATO armies, and Bundeswehr tactical networking is contracted through 2029 (E06-F13). No CIHBw TAK pilot was found in public sources this session.
allied_extension.what_changes: Entity structure (a NATO-nation-domiciled entity for DIANA; dual-jurisdiction cost, E07-F34), export posture (any integration/training for a foreign military can be an ITAR defense service even for EAR99 software - E07-F15 proposed rule, no final rule confirmed; counsel required before a Bundeswehr or other foreign-military pilot), data schemas (NATO APP-11 message formats and national report formats replace NIMS ICS forms - a second schema pack, not a new product), and the buyer (civil-protection agencies such as German THW/fire services and allied light units on ATAK rather than U.S. IMTs). The German founder's language and network access to CIHBw is the only concrete advantage.

kill_criteria: KILL if after 15 interviews zero budget holders (state TAK program lead, fire chief, EOC manager, SAA) can name a fund and a fiscal year from which they would pay for this - not 'would be interested'

KILL if no former IC/PSC-level advisor agrees to participate by end of Week 3 (score file: fatal-if-absent)

goals: Prove the technical wedge is cheap: CRDT-merged ICS objects transported as mission deltas through an unmodified TAK Server / OpenTAKServer mission API
Decide iOS strategy empirically (web companion/PWA vs. Meshtastic iOS TAK-server path) since iTAK has no plugin architecture
deliverables: Bench experiment: 5 Android EUDs (ATAK-CIV) + 1 laptop ICP + 1 web companion on iOS, 4 deliberate partitions, multi-writer edits to the same ICS 204 assignment and resource quantities; report convergence time, bytes per object, conflicts surfaced vs. auto-merged
Meshtastic/LoRa transport test of object deltas (message size budget, loss behavior)
Decision memo: Automerge/Yjs/custom merge choice with per-field semantics (LWW with causal history for text, list merge for assignments, explicit conflict surfacing for quantities)
Public GitHub repository with README, license and reproducible test harness

kill_criteria: KILL the CRDT-object thesis if the mission API cannot carry object deltas without forking TAK Server (i.e., the extension would require a TPC-controlled server change)

KILL if by end of Week 6 no state TAK program or IMT has agreed in writing to a no-cost pilot window in Q1-Q2 2027

Show it at CivTAK 2026 (Nov 18-20) and record buyer reactions
deliverables: Installable prototype v0.2 (APK, server container, web companion) with a 10-minute scripted partition-and-merge demo
CivTAK 2026 demo delivered to at least 15 public-safety TAK administrators and at least one TPC Data Sync engineer; structured notes on each

Decide go/no-go on continuing beyond 90 days with a written case

kill_criteria: KILL if the prototype does not cut ICS 204 production time by at least 30% versus paper/Word in the moderated session, or if any merge produces a lost or duplicated assignment

KILL if total credible 12-month pipeline is below $50k ARR - at that level the correct decision is to hand the open-source project to TAK Public Safety/WFTAK stewardship and approach Ditto, a TPC contractor or an IMS vendor about an acquihire
Regardless of outcome: do not raise outside capital on this version; it is a bootstrapped niche business or an acquihire, and the plan's own evidence cannot justify a venture round

most_important_question.build_first: An open-source TAK Server/OpenTAKServer extension plus ATAK-CIV plugin plus a thin web companion (for the iOS majority, since iTAK has no plugin architecture) that stores three things as CRDT-merged Data Sync mission objects: ICS 204 assignments, ICS 214 activity/status entries, and a resource/LOGSTAT-style ledger with per-field merge semantics (LWW-with-history for text, list merge for assignments, explicit conflict surfacing for quantities), transported as compact mission deltas over Meshtastic/LoRa and FirstNet. Roughly $50k and 90 days to a demonstrable prototype; entirely unclassified, EAR99-by-design, buildable by the non-U.S.-person founder. Nothing military-specific in v1.
most_important_question.show_it_to: In order: (1) the state wildland TAK program lead who runs a WFTAK-using or COTAK-type server, (2) a Type 2 IMT planning section chief and resource unit leader, (3) the TAK Product Center Data Sync engineer at CivTAK 2026 (Nov 18-20, DC), (4) an SAA grants manager and an agency budget analyst, (5) a Guard battalion S3 on a drill weekend as an unfunded dual-use check. Not to Army program offices, not to DIU, not to primes - that buyer has been ceded to SBMC/Onebrief.
most_important_question.demo_proves: That edits to the same assignment, activity log and resource quantities made by multiple users during a >=4-hour partition merge on reconnect with zero re-keying, zero lost or duplicated records, on Android and on iOS via the web companion, over a LoRa mesh at under 20 KB per edit; and that a planning section produces the next operational period's ICS 204s at least 30% faster than on paper/Word. It deliberately does NOT try to prove a merge model worth licensing - that thesis is dead.
most_important_question.why_customer_cares: Every operational period the planning section re-keys assignments and status from radio, paper and chat; every reconnect after a division worked disconnected forces a manual reconcile of which version is current; the IC defends numbers he or she cannot trace. The product removes the re-keying and makes provenance visible inside the TAK app the agency already runs. Caveat from the score file: the pain is real but tolerated (severity 3/5), and TAK Public Safety's own charter says adoption is gated by training, not features - the 90-day plan tests whether the pain is worth $5k-$20k a year to anyone.
most_important_question.why_incumbent_cant_crush: Honest answer: they can. TPC can add form objects to free Data Sync; Ditto can ship a schema pack on its ATAK plugin; Resgrid already markets offline-first ICS-201; Tablet Command/Intterra/WebEOC own agency relationships; the schemas are public standards and the merge engine is open source. The only partial defenses are (a) speed and focus - none of them has combined structured ICS objects + multi-writer merge + TAK-native, and public-safety vendors move slowly; (b) open-source community stewardship with TAK Public Safety/WFTAK so that the de facto 'ICS objects for TAK' schema is the company's, making the company the natural maintainer/hosting provider and the natural acquihire; (c) the founders' cost base (two students) lets a $100k-ARR business survive where a funded vendor would not bother. These are reasons a small business can exist, not reasons a venture can win - which is why the verdict is kill-as-venture.
most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m: Twenty or more paying agencies or one statewide enterprise contract (>= $150k ARR combined) within 12 months of CivTAK 2026, plus written evidence that TPC will not add form objects natively, plus a signed integration or acquisition LOI from an IMS vendor, Ditto or a TPC contractor. The plan's own evidence says this milestone is unlikely: agency ACVs are low five figures, the buying cycle is 12-24 months, and the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for what it can take from open source. If the milestone is missed, the correct next step is not a raise but stewardship transfer plus acquihire outreach. If it is somehow hit, $2-5M would fund a SLED sales lead, StateRAMP/security packaging and a second schema pack (NATO/allied civil protection) - still a small-cap outcome.
